codecVersion: *** Zstandard CLI (64-bit) v1.5.7, by Yann Collet ***
note: Local Zstd is a layout filter, not a replacement for Roblox Stats.DataSendKbps.

notes.blink: Blink generated client: [id u8][u16 count][u16 lengths plane][string bytes] per event. Id 3 comes from the generated tags: Vectors 2, Strings 3, Mixed 4.
notes.blinkblox: BlinkBlox v1.3.6 generated client: [id u8][varint count][u8 length, characters each] per event, id 3 from the generated writer. Reliable fires batch per frame but the 64-event / 8192-byte packet cuts fall on RemoteEvent boundaries and add no bytes, so the frame model is the concatenated events.
notes.courier: Courier v0.2.0 generated implementation: per fire a 3-bit tag, an alignment hold to the byte boundary past the cursor plus ten bits, a 7-bit count leaf and 100 six-bit length leaves, little-endian in one continuous bit stream; the content rides the tail region the compiler packs descending from the frame end, so it reads later fires and later strings first. The model follows the mode accounting (bit area + content tail) and excludes the 20-byte internal stream header.
notes.jolt: Jolt v4.4.1 source: records concatenate with no outer frame, head [u16 channel hash][u8 (packetType << 6 | argCount)] rides with every fire, then the string array argument [43][varInt count][u8 length, characters each]. The u16 hash is FNV-1a of the channel name folded to 16 bits, computed inline above.
notes.lync: Lync v4.0.3 source: reliable blocks ride one u8 head (3-bit def id, 5-bit run count). The Strings def rides id 4 with the run count zero, because each payload can span the whole 3301-byte room ceiling and seals its own block. Bodies are the biased (len - 8) length byte plus the characters per string, no array-level count on the fixed array.
notes.netray_compile: NetRay-Compile v0.2.0: fixedarray<string(8, 32), 100> bodies drop the array count, per string the biased (len - 8) u8 length then the characters, behind one same-id run header [u8 segment marker 0][u8 event id 4][varUInt run count] per flushed frame. The June row carried a varUInt value count per event because the v0.1.1 schema had a dynamic array.
notes.quicknet: QuickNet v0.4.0 source: one frame per batch is [u16 numCalls], each call is [u8 actionId][u16 count][u8 length][bytes]. Strings register with data.String, which is a u8 length, not the u16 length the Benchmarks.md wire estimate assumed, so this row reads lower than the tilde line. actionId is taken from register order (0-based), a constant byte.
notes.virtualnet: VirtualNet v0.1.2 source: one packed batch per flushed frame carries a 7-byte head (count u32, packet id u16, packed flag) followed by the event bodies with no per-event prefix. The fixed array emits no array count and the 255 cap gives one u8 length per string, so the body is 100 x (u8 length + characters) per event. The batch is never transposed (setTranspose is not called in the benchmark mode) and transport-level packing is not modeled: the mode reports body bytes only and adds the head outside its totals, so this row is the modeled list over counted regions: the head is included here once per frame.
notes.warp: Warp 1.1.0-pre8 (R3 swap from the June 1.1.0-pre7 copy): one per-direction Xor packet per flushed frame, two head bytes (kind + sequence) ahead of varUInt(event count), then [id u8][varUInt count][u8 length][bytes] per event. Delta packets XOR the payload region against the previous packet's payload and the keyframe interval is one second, so at a 60 Hz tick every 60th frame rides verbatim. Id 5 assumes the alphabetical bench children order; the id is a constant byte, so sizes do not depend on it.
